body:
## Summary

Parsing numbers from contiguous input scanned every digit twice. `scan_number_bulk_contiguous()` validated the token one byte at a time and copied it into `token_buffer`. The conversion then went through two out-of-line functions that read the digits again:

- `parse_float_native()` called `parse_float_significand()`, which returned its result through memory and called `std::any_of` twice per number (GCC does not inline it).
- `parse_integer_signed()` divided by ten on every digit for its overflow check.

This PR accumulates the value while the digits are validated:

- Digits are taken **eight at a time** where at least eight bytes remain: `is_eight_digits()` tests them and `parse_eight_digits()` converts them, as in fast_float.
- **Floats with at most 19 digits** go straight to `decimal_to_float()` (Clinger's fast path or Eisel–Lemire), so the float fast path has no calls left.
- **Integers with at most 18 digits** are stored without an overflow check. A narrower `number_integer_t`/`number_unsigned_t` still rejects values that do not round-trip, as before.
- **Longer tokens, and float formats other than binary32/binary64** (e.g. x87 `long double`), take the existing path. It is unchanged, except that `has_nonzero_digit()` is now a plain loop and `parse_float_significand()` is always inlined.

The stream windows of #5828 are handled like the existing fast path: a number that reaches the end of a window falls back to `scan_number()`, and the terminator is read and ungotten.

This is the first of five stacked PRs from an assembly review of the number and string parsing; the stack is based on #5828.

## Performance

Change of the best-of-runs time against the previous PR (the first: against #5828), negative is faster. *accept* is `json::accept()` (no allocations), *parse* is `json::parse()`. Apple M1 Max: Apple Clang 21 and Homebrew GCC 16; x86-64 (Haswell VM): GCC 13, and Clang 18 with `-falign-loops=64 -falign-functions=64` on both sides (without it, code placement alone moves Clang's numbers by up to ±5 % between builds). Improvements of 3 % or more are bold.

| file | M1 Clang accept | M1 Clang parse | M1 GCC 16 accept | M1 GCC 16 parse | x86 GCC accept | x86 Clang accept |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `canada.json` | **−18.8 %** | **−9.8 %** | **−17.2 %** | **−9.3 %** | **−11.5 %** | **−20.7 %** |
| `citm_catalog.json` | **−6.8 %** | **−3.0 %** | **−8.3 %** | −1.9 % | −1.3 % | +3.1 % |
| `twitter.json` | −0.3 % | −0.3 % | −1.0 % | +0.1 % | +4.7 % | +0.8 % |
| `numbers.json` | **−25.1 %** | **−22.7 %** | **−20.4 %** | **−20.1 %** | **−18.4 %** | **−24.7 %** |
| `long_strings.json` | −0.2 % | +1.6 % | −1.9 % | −1.6 % | −1.4 % | +0.7 % |
| `twitterescaped.json` | −0.7 % | +0.1 % | −0.9 % | −0.3 % | +6.4 % | +1.0 % |
| `mesh.json` | **−18.6 %** | **−13.5 %** | **−14.9 %** | **−12.4 %** | **−13.7 %** | **−16.1 %** |

This PR does not touch the string code; the x86-64 GCC rows for twitter.json and twitterescaped.json (+5 to +6 %) come from code placement and from the shared machine, which was under load during this run (the M1 rows for these files are within ±1 %).

## Tests

- **New section "digits accumulated while scanning"** in `unit-class_lexer.cpp`:
  - covers every digit count from 1 to 25, in the integer and the fraction part, with and without sign and exponent, with leading zeros, and with exponents beyond every range;
  - compares each case with the byte path. The reference input is a `std::list<char>`: since #5828, a `std::stringstream` takes the bulk path as well, so it is no longer an independent reference.
- **New section for narrower number types:** a `basic_json` with 32-bit integers checks the round-trip check.
- **Mutation check:** raising either digit limit by one makes these tests fail.
- **Differential check against #5828's head:** identical DOM output, error messages, `accept()` results and SAX events (including the float text), for 737 files of json_test_data and 500k generated inputs. Each input is parsed from a string, an `std::istream` and a `FILE*`. Run on Apple M1 (Clang) and x86-64 (GCC 13, Clang 18).
- **Full test suite:** passes under ASan/UBSan on macOS (Clang) and Linux x86-64 (GCC).

## Breaking changes

None. Only internal functions in `nlohmann::detail` change. Values, exceptions and error positions are the same, as the differential check above shows.

review_comments.body: Is this repeated code that could use a helper?

Yes, though not quite this loop: the integer part and the fraction in `parse_float_significand()` ran the same eight-digits-then-one-digit loop. In 2dfda27f2 they share `accumulate_significant_digits()`, and clang -O2 emits the same code as before. `accumulate_digits()` stays separate because it checks each byte for a digit and has no 19-digit cap, so a shared helper would need both as parameters.

— posted by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann

title: Accumulate number digits while scanning them
